errors.text: The proposed temperature and strain-rate domains differ fundamentally from the target: conventional rates of 10^-4–10^-1 s^-1 and 77–1073 K replace molecular-dynamics rates of 10^8–10^10 s^-1 and 10–600 K.

It attributes rate insensitivity to edge-dislocation glide and a 673–873 K thermal plateau, whereas the target mechanism is nucleation and glide of Shockley partials with stacking-fault formation over the simulated rate range.
The supporting evidence is primarily from refractory BCC alloys and does not establish edge-dislocation-controlled yielding or strain-rate insensitivity in FCC FeNiCrMn.
The cited high-temperature strength plateau concerns strength versus temperature and is not evidence that yield strength is insensitive to strain rate.
Cryogenic deformation twinning is predicted despite the target finding no twinning and deformation through partial dislocations and stacking faults.
The hypothesis omits the target's single-crystal crystallographic orientation dependence, vacancy-assisted nucleation, and maximum yield stress along the <-111> direction.
